transcript:
This message comes from Capital One with the Venture X Card.
Earn unlimited double miles and a $300 annual Capital One travel credit.
Capital One.
What's in your wallet?
Terms of fly.
Details at CapitalOne.com.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
World leaders from the group of seven countries say they've agreed to release 100 million
barrels of oil and fuel products starting with substantial amounts of diesel after the
fuel recently hit record high prices in the U.S., President Trump says he asked for it.
He's facing pressure to address surging prices ahead of November's midterm elections.
New York Democratic Governor Kathy Hochul says she wants answers about why an alleged
rape case at Cornell University wasn't fully investigated, NPR's Brian Mann reports.
Hochul says she's troubled by the behavior of university leaders, campus police, and
a local prosecutor who dropped the investigation two years ago after seeing only a partial transcript
of the woman's allegations.
I will not allow anyone to sweep this case under the rug.
Letitia James, the state attorney general, will now take over the criminal probe.
Hochul says she'll also push to close a loophole in state law that makes it harder to prosecute
sex crimes when the victim has been drinking or using drugs.
Voluntary intoxication is not a license for sexual assault or gang rape, period.
Cornell University has also agreed to Hochul's demand that an outside counsel review the school's
handling of the case.
Brian Mann, NPR News, Ithaca, New York.
Krista Pike's attorneys say she's still in a hospital unconscious and on a ventilator
after her failed execution in Tennessee on Wednesday.
Pike was sentenced to death for a murder she committed at age 18.
She would have been the first woman executed in Tennessee in more than 200 years.
Republican Governor Bill Lee has ordered an independent review and paused executions.
This week, the Trump administration began mailing out $500 checks to nearly one million
Americans enrolled in certain private health insurance plans.
As NPR's Selena Simmons-Duffin reports, the money comes from fees collected from health
insurance companies.
The group of people receiving the checks live in one of the 30 states that use HealthCare.gov
as their Obamacare website and make too much money to receive premium subsidies.
Cynthia Cox directs the program on the Affordable Care Act at the health research organization
KFF.
"Essentially what the Trump administration is doing is taking some user fee dollars that
insurance companies have paid to the federal government to operate HealthCare.gov."
Usually, that money is used for community groups who help people understand their options
and enroll, but the Trump administration has slashed funding for those groups and is now
sending out checks instead.
Selena Simmons-Duffin, NPR News, Washington.
This year's Kennedy Center honors will be held at Washington, D.C.'s Capital One Arena
instead of the usual Riverfront Performing Arts venue.
The change comes after the center's Trump-friendly board voted to close the iconic venue after
a judge blocked plans to add President Trump's name.
Trump has claimed the center needs safety repairs, which he says will only happen if
his name is added.
U.S. stocks rose near their record highs today.
This is NPR News from Washington.
Hurricane Rachel has been upgraded to a Category 3 storm off of Mexico's Pacific Coast.
Its swells are expected to generate life-threatening surf.
Northern Mexico and parts of the U.S. Southwest are still dealing with flooding and damage
from Hurricane Polo earlier this week.
The deal to merge Paramount's Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery is expected to finalize
next week, NPR's Mondalee Del Barco reports.
With help from his billionaire father Larry Ellison and investors from Saudi Arabia, Qatar,
and others, David Ellison will soon have control over his mega-company, which he named Skydance.
Ellison is spending more than $111 billion to combine two legacy film studios, streaming
companies and news outlets CNN and CBS News.
Ellison posted this video on X and wrote that Skydance will allow Paramount and Warner Bros.
to continue their individual identities.
Despite protests from actors, writers, and others, and after passing legal and regulatory
challenges, the deal is expected to close on Tuesday.
Mondalee Del Barco, NPR News, Los Angeles.
Basketball star Caitlin Clark's new signature sneakers sold out in two hours on Nike's website,
according to CNBC. Nike's CEO says the Caitlin ones were launched in 5,000 retail stores,
the largest signature shoe launch in the company's history. Clark's Indiana Fever were eliminated
from the 2026 WNBA playoffs last night after losing to the Las Vegas aces in the first
round.
This is NPR News.
